currency_exchange How the Premium Market works

You define the general settings, register the rotation villages and create per-village exceptions whenever you want. If the current village is registered, the main screen then edits its own settings.

scheduleAutomatic checking
shopping_cartBuy within target
sellSell within target
shopping_cart

Buy

Buys when the real rate is ≥ minimum rate you defined. Rate = resources received ÷ points spent. The higher, the better for you.

Example: target rate 80 → the script only buys if it receives at least 80 resources per point.
sell

Sell

Sells when the real rate is ≤ maximum rate you defined. Rate = resources spent ÷ points received. The lower, the better for you.

Example: target rate 100 → the script only sells if it spends at most 100 resources per point.
tune

Where to edit each thing

1
Main screen If the current village is registered in Villages, clicking Save here creates or updates its own settings. If it is not registered, saving changes the general settings.
2
Automatic overrides When you save from the main screen of a registered village, the script stores only the difference from the general settings. If a value becomes equal to the general one again, that override disappears.
3
Villages popup Use the Villages button to set up the rotation, add or removes villages and create, clear or review per-village settings.
Summary: everything not overridden by a village keeps inheriting the general settings.
auto_awesome

How Automatic mode decides

query_statsBest rate Picks the resource with the best resources-per-point ratio within the configured target.
priority_highGreatest need When buying, prioritizes the resource with the lowest current amount in the village.
stacked_bar_chartGreatest surplus When selling, prioritizes the resource with the largest surplus above the configured reserve.
Important: the automatic strategy only kicks in when the priority is set to Auto.
storage

How it works inside

1
Reads the market Every cycle, the script fetches current market data and recalculates buy and sell opportunities.
2
Applies your rules Target rate, active resources, chosen priority, minimum reserve and available capacity all feed the decision.
3
Runs safely Cross-tab protection avoids conflicts, the rate is verified before confirmation and the reserve prevents selling below the defined minimum.
Tip: use a faster frequency only when you want to compete for better rates. Very high frequencies increase the number of requests to the server.

help How Overwatch works

What it shows on the map

Overwatch marks only your villages. Each village gets a color and briefly shows the configured population, the wall, optional loyalty, the defense flag when it exists and is enabled, attack alerts when enabled and the paladin when present.

How to read the colors

Colors follow the population ranges you set in the panel. When a village's displayed population goes up or down, the color automatically changes to the matching range.

Add incoming support

When this option is on, the total shown on the map also counts support still on its way to the village. The first load may take a bit longer on accounts with many incomings.

Defense fill

Use the Defense fill toggle to turn on map selection. The Open panel button only opens the modal. You can close the panel and keep clicking your villages on the map without losing the selection.

Defense fill outputs

The panel can generate two outputs: Text, to paste into mass support, and BBCode/table, to share on a forum or chat. The Arrival until option is global and goes into every line of the current output.

Refresh list

Refresh list reapplies the current default to all saved villages and then refreshes the data. This is useful when you redefine the defense target and want to propagate the change without removing and adding the villages again.

When to use Update and Clear cache

Use Update after moving troops, receiving support or changing the ranges. Use Clear cache if incoming support looks outdated; the next read may be slower because Overwatch will fetch everything again.

Configure population

In Configure pop, you choose which units count and how much each is worth. This changes the number shown on the map, influences the range colors and also affects the incoming support sum.

Resources mode

When Show resources and warehouse is on, Overwatch swaps the population mode for one focused on wood, clay and iron. In this mode, incoming support and loyalty are hidden for a cleaner read, but flags and alerts keep following your toggles.

Icons and quick info

Farm: total shown by Overwatch. Wall: current level. Flag: defense flag image when the toggle is on. Red badge: number of incoming attacks when the toggle is on. Green paladin: in the village. Yellow paladin: arriving as support. If loyalty cannot be read on the current account, it shows as --.

<div class=\"gc-flags-help-floating-head:
How does the Flags Auto GC work?close

Auto GC organizes your villages in stages, in the order: Defense → Attack → Population → Recruitment → Utilities. Each stage uses the chosen groups and applies the flag starting from the highest level down to the configured minimum.

  • Attack and Population accept multiple groups — they are used in the order they appear.
  • A village that already has the stage's own flag is skipped.
  • Coin and population flags are never swapped by the other stages; the rest can be replaced.
  • Villages in the Blocklist groups are left out of everything.
  • A village already handled in one stage is not repeated in the following ones.

Metrics for each card: Read = villages analyzed; Eligible = ready to receive the flag; Protected = preserved; Correct = already with the right flag; Assigned = changed; Pending = not completed.

Coin flags give a discount on coin costs. In this automation they are always protected and never swapped.

How does the Paladin work?close

The menu brings paladin training and education together in one place:

  • Training: enable the desired paladins and set for each one:
    • Max lv: Trains until reaching that level — when it does, it stops automatically.
    • Stop: Deadline date/time — if the training would finish after that time, it does not start. Useful to free the paladin before an operation.
    • Cut with PP ⚡: Uses PP to reduce training time. Set how many minutes you want left — if the remaining time is greater than that value, the script calls rush in a loop until it reaches it. Works immediately when training starts and also in later cycles if already training.
  • Education: on each card, enable the paladin and choose a teaching template — inventory books are used in order up to the target level. With Automatic Education on, the cycle runs every 30 minutes (15 minutes in aggressive mode).
  • Templates: teaching plans with the order and target level (1 to 4) of each book. Default templates can be duplicated and edited freely.

Training always uses the cheapest available training and only starts if the base village has enough resources.

<div class=\"mpd-help-head\"> <span clas:
campaign How the Defense Notice works
campaign What it does
  • bolt When the Tagger identifies a command with a noble arriving at one of your villages, this script builds an automatic PM with everything the tribe needs to decide whether to support.
  • person The PM goes out in your name, with no bot signature, a few seconds after tagging. It does nothing on its own besides notifying.
groups Who receives it
  • groups Tribe: players from your tribe with a village inside the radius (fields slider), sorted by distance — closest first.
  • person Nicks: manual list of players. They also only receive if they have a village inside the radius, same as the tribe.
  • block You and the attacker never receive it.
  • travel_explore Use Simulate recipients with any coordinate to see exactly who would receive it (and who would be left out, with the reason).
schedule When it notifies
  • timer Wait (30s to 15min): time between detecting the noble and sending the PM, so the train appears complete before the notice.
  • directions_railway Noble train only: when on, it only notifies when 3 or more nobles arrive with up to 2s between them. An isolated noble does not generate a PM.
  • folder_open Monitored group: only generates a notice for attacks on villages of the selected group ("all" = all your villages).
  • hourglass_top Per-village cooldown: minimum interval between PMs for the same village, to avoid repeating the notice when new nobles arrive after the first.
  • call_merge Several villages attacked in the same round become a single PM with one section per village.
mail What goes in the message
  • timeline Timeline in arrival order with all attacks on the village (ram/spy fakes show the unit icon) and the support between the nobles and after the train — support after the train is limited to 10, the rest is summarized in one line.
  • shield Wall, loyalty and current defense (you can hide the defense in the "Message sent" card).
verified_user Guarantees
  • link The script only works with the Tagger enabled (activation itself is blocked without it).
  • send Send test to me sends the sample message only to you, to validate the format.
  • history The history shows the latest sends: the coordinate opens the village and the recipients open the profile — always in a new tab.

help_outline Ajuda — Aba de Apoio

shield Troop settings
filter_alt Minimum — minimum amount the village must have to appear in the list. The village must meet all the defined minimums to be included.
send Send — amount of troops to send per support command from each village.
select_all Tudo — sends all available troops of that unit. The "Send" field is ignored for that unit.
functions Total — sets the desired global total for each unit. The script stops adding villages once the troop sum reaches this value. The last village may receive less to hit the total exactly. If zero, there is no limit.
schedule Timing
event Arrival — time at which all supports must arrive at the target. Each village departs at a different time depending on distance.
timer Delay (ms) — milliseconds added (+) or subtracted (-) from each support's departure time. Values from 0 to 300ms.
speed Affliction % — reduces the support travel time. World value (0 to 60%). The higher, the faster the support arrives.
alarm_add Paste time — the 🕐 button next to the date field pastes a time from the clipboard (formats: HH:mm:ss, HH:mm:ss.SSS, etc.).
chess_pawn Regra do Paladino
warning When the Paladino is included in a support command, it sets the travel time — regardless of other troops. Even if the other units are faster or slower, the paladin's speed prevails, including in the filter Troops by speed (all units are evaluated at its speed). This is a game rule applied automatically by the script.
balance Distribution mode
trending_up Maximum — each village sends up to the "Send" value (or everything, if checked). Good to concentrate maximum troops per command.
balance Equilibrada — splits troops evenly across all qualified villages. Good to spread the support load.
tune Filters and options
sort Ordem — "Nearest" sends from the closest villages first; "Farthest" prioritizes distant ones.
format_list_numbered Limite de comandos — limits the number of supports in the table (1 to 500).
event_busy Deduct already scheduled troops — subtracts troops from pending commands in the scheduler, showing only what is really available.
speed Troops by speed — evaluates each unit type individually. If light cavalry arrives in time but the axe fighter does not, only light cavalry is sent. With the Paladino in the support, all units are evaluated at its speed (paladin rule). The minimum filters per unit (does not drop the whole village). The send field caps the maximum; if empty, sends everything available. Accounts for affliction in the time calculation.
delete_sweep Limpar Filtros — resets all troop fields, filters and settings, and clears the results table.
table_chart Tabela de Resultados
link Origin — clickable coordinate that opens the village in a new tab. The name shows below.
military_tech Apoio — icons and troop amounts to send. Hover to see the exact value.
update Departing in — live countdown. Turns red when less than 5 minutes remain.
check_box Selected total — sum of troops of the checked commands, shown in the table footer.
dashboard Painel de Overview
visibility Above the results table, a summary of commands already scheduled for the target village is shown: number of attacks, supports and total committed troops.
warning Late commands
schedule_send If some commands have departures already in the past when scheduling, a window appears with 3 options:
⏭️ Pular atrasados Schedules only the commands still within the deadline.
📋 Schedule all Schedules everything, including late ones. The scheduler sends the overdue ones immediately.
❌ Cancel Cancels the scheduling. No command is saved.

Advanced settings
close
Time settings
Default send offset
Fine-tune in milliseconds to compensate latency
ms
Send precision mode
Como o script corrige a hora do envio para compensar o atraso da internet. Tradicional usa o valor fixo do campo acima. Adaptativo measures the delay of recent commands and adjusts itself — recommended for most cases.
Estilo de Ajuste Adaptive mode only
Responsivo reacts quickly to delay changes (ideal in most cases). Stable keeps the adjustment steadier and ignores short variations, useful on unstable connections.
Correction cap Adaptive mode only
Cap of the compensation applied by the script. Delays above the selected value are considered bugs e ignorados.
Lead time to open tab
Lead time to open the command tab
segundos
Default cancellation time
Default time between send and cancellation for cancellation/NT commands. Does not affect auto dodge, which computes the return from received attacks. (Min: 15s, Máx: 540s)
segundos
Dodge departure lead time
How many seconds in advance auto dodge pulls troops from the village before the first attack lands. If the attack is closer, it uses all available time. Increase it when many dodges share the same time, to give room to send every command. On worlds with a short cancellation window, high values are automatically reduced to the maximum allowed and may split a sequence into more than one dodge. (Min: 15s, Máx: 540s)
segundos
Reorder gap
Milliseconds of difference when dragging a command below another in the table.
ms
Automatic calibration
Calibrar Offset
In traditional mode, stores the measured offset and updates pending commands. In adaptive mode, updates the delay reference.
Fake optimization
Deduzir Fakes de Attacks Full
When enabled, upon validating a "full" attack, the script looks for pending fakes (attacks within the fake limit and without nobles) from the same village. Those fake troops are reserved, and the "full" attack is sent with the remaining units.
Minimum population for a "full" attack
Defines what a "full" attack is. Only commands with population equal to or above this value trigger the optimization and deduct pending fake troops.
pop
Maximum population for fakes
Sets the maximum population a command may have to be considered a "fake" during deduction.
pop
Modelos de Fake

Defines fake types. The first template in the list is the default. These templates are shared with the mail importer.

Comportamento de Envio
Open new tabs for sending
Lets the scheduler automatically open a new tab to fire commands. If you disable this, commands are sent using the current tab, but keeping the rally point screen open is strictly required para funcionar.
Interface do Visualizador
Items per page (list)
Sets how many commands are shown per page in list view.
itens
Coluna Player (Target)
Shows the target village's owner in the viewer. Disabling speeds up opening the viewer (skips village/player maps). Search by name still works.
Funcionalidades de Tela
Quick Scheduler
Enables a quick scheduling panel (nobles, attacks and supports) right on the village overview screen.
Nexus Overview
Enables Nexus Overview metrics on the combined overviews screen, showing panels and scheduled command counts.
Advanced mass scheduling NOVO!
Enables the new mass scheduling, with far more options and smarter, more efficient scheduling.
Auto-Max Commands por Target
When changing origins or targets in mass scheduling, fills the "commands per target" field with the maximum possible.
Separar Data e Hora MOBILE
Replaces the single date/time field with separate date and time fields (typeable). Ideal for scheduling on mobile, where the native picker makes entering minutes and seconds hard.
Agendador no Popup do Mapa
Enables individual scheduling directly in the attack/support popup opened from the map. When disabled, the scheduler no longer appears in the popup, but the queue keeps processing commands.
Nexus no Popup de Origin
Shows a Nexus column on the map popup's "choose an origin" screen, listing each village's scheduled commands with a details tooltip and filters.
Alertas e Avisos
Pending commands alert
Shows a corner notification when commands are scheduled to leave the current village. Clicking it takes you straight to the viewer, pre-filtered.
